item.text: I found a cohesive simulator-level refactor with better payoff than another local cleanup: `Simulator` still defines species data in three separate places, with duplicated probabilities, colors, and constructor wiring. I’m consolidating that into one species registry so spawning and color registration come from the same source of truth.
I’m editing `Simulator` now to replace the split constants with one declarative registry. That should remove the probability/color duplication and make adding or changing a species a one-line change.
The registry refactor is in place. I’m compiling now to verify the consolidated species definitions still drive both population setup and view colors correctly.
The compile passed. I’m pulling the final line references from `Simulator` so I can close this refactor out cleanly.

Refactored [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/Simulator.java:21) so species configuration now lives in one registry instead of three separate blocks of probabilities, colors, and spawn rules. The new `SpeciesDefinition` list at [Simulator.java](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/Simulator.java:47) is now the single source of truth for each species’ class, initial spawn probability, color, and construction logic.

That lets both initial population creation and view color registration iterate the same definitions. [createInitialActor()](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/Simulator.java:252) now uses the registry directly, and [registerViewColors()](/Users/allenjiang/Documents/ACE-Sycophancy-Codebase-Dataset/_worktrees/R003_module_java/Simulator.java:277) no longer needs a separate hard-coded mapping. The result is less drift risk and a much smaller edit surface when adding or tuning species.
